openItems.explanation: Cedar Hollow Tile (V-109) gave a W-9 with the business name on line 1 and an SSN as a sole proprietor; IRS TIN Matching found no match. Form W-9 asks a sole proprietor for the owner's name on line 1 and the business name on line 2. The draft reports $26,850.00 under the name and TIN on file. A person gets the corrected W-9 before filing; filed as is, the form is likely to draw an IRS notice and a B notice, after which backup withholding would apply.

Ridgeline Concrete Cutting (V-108) never gave a W-9 or a TIN. 24% backup withholding was due on all 5 payments, $3,456.00; accounts payable withheld $2,112.00 from April 30 on, reported in box 4. The $1,344.00 not withheld from February 27 and March 31 is HANGS's own liability. A person reports the backup withholding on Form 945 and keeps soliciting the TIN; the form is filed with the TIN box blank.

Tomas Arvelo, an individual, was paid $33,348.00 through accounts payable in 2026 for 794 hours of concrete finishing at $42.00 an hour under the HGC foreman, the question left open by the Q3 Form 941 review. The draft reports a Form 1099-NEC as accounts payable recorded the work. If a person decides the work is employment, the pay belongs on a Form W-2 with withholding instead, and the payroll returns change.

Two payees belong on Form 1099-MISC, which this run does not prepare: $96,000.00 of office rent to Harbor Ridge Office Partners LLC (box 1), and the $85,000.00 settlement paid to Moss and Tarrant PLLC (box 10, gross proceeds paid to an attorney). Form 1099-MISC has its own dates: e-filed with the IRS by March 31, 2027.

Unsigned draft. The 9 Forms 1099-NEC are due to the IRS and to the recipients by Monday, February 1, 2027 (January 31 is a Sunday). HANGS must e-file; no Form 1096 is filed with an electronic filing. Resolve TIN-01 and LABOR-01 first; a person reviews, e-files and sends the recipient copies. Nothing has been filed.

rules.question: What is the 2026 threshold for Form 1099-NEC, and did it change?
rules.whyItMatters: Payments below the threshold need no Form 1099-NEC. For payments made in 2026 the threshold rose from $600 to $2,000.
rules.effective: Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026), What's New.
rules.excerpt: For tax years beginning after 2025, the minimum threshold amount for reporting certain payments required to be reported on certain information returns and/or perform backup withholding on those payments increased to $2,000 and may be adjusted for inflation beginning in calendar year 2027. ... Enter nonemployee compensation (NEC) of $2,000 or more.
matchPhrases: for tax years beginning after 2025, the minimum threshold amount for reporting certain payments required to be reported on certain information returns and/or perform backup withholding on those payments increased to $2,000
enter nonemployee compensation (nec) of $2,000 or more
to whom you have paid at least $2,000 in: services performed by someone who is not your employee (including parts and materials)
rules.pageOrSection: What's New: Increase in threshold; Specific Instructions for Form 1099-NEC; Box 1a
rules.ruleOrLimit: File Form 1099-NEC for each payee paid at least $2,000 in 2026 for services, parts and materials included. Through 2025 the threshold was $600.
rules.hangsApplication: Two sole proprietors were paid for services under $2,000: Wen Iverson (Bayview Locksmith) $1,450.00 and Omar Kettering (Rainier Window Cleaning) $1,980.00. Under the $600 threshold both would have been reported; for 2026 neither is. Talia Brannigan (Northwest Safety Training) was paid exactly $2,000.00 and is reported.

rules.question: When are the 2026 Forms 1099-NEC due, and must they be e-filed?
rules.whyItMatters: Form 1099-NEC has one date for the IRS and the recipients, and paper is not allowed for a payer filing 10 or more information returns.
rules.excerpt: Section 6071(c) requires you to file Form 1099-NEC on or before January 31, using either paper or electronic filing procedures. ... If any date shown falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday ... the due date is the next business day. ... lowered the e-file threshold to 10 (calculated by aggregating all information returns)
matchPhrases: section 6071(c) requires you to file form 1099-nec on or before january 31, using either paper or electronic filing procedures
if any date shown falls on a saturday, sunday, or legal holiday in the district of columbia or where the return is to be filed, the due date is the next business day
lowered the e-file threshold to 10 (calculated by aggregating all information returns)
rules.pageOrSection: Reminders: Filing dates; What's New: E-filing returns
rules.ruleOrLimit: Form 1099-NEC is due to the IRS and to each recipient by January 31, moved to the next business day. A payer with 10 or more information returns in all must e-file.
rules.hangsApplication: January 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so the forms are due Monday, February 1, 2027. With 101 Forms W-2 and these 9 Forms 1099-NEC, HANGS files well over 10 information returns and must e-file, through IRIS as its payer details say.
hangsFactsUsed: Payer details (information returns and filing method)
rules.unresolved: Unsigned draft; a person reviews, e-files and sends the recipient copies (RETURN-01).

rules.question: Is a Form 1096 needed?
rules.whyItMatters: Form 1096 transmits paper forms only. An electronic filing carries its own totals.
rules.excerpt: Use Form 1096 to transmit paper Forms 1097, 1098, 1099, 3921, 3922, 5498, and W-2G to the Internal Revenue Service. Do not use this form to transmit electronically.
matchPhrases: use form 1096 to transmit paper forms 1097, 1098, 1099, 3921, 3922, 5498, and w-2g to the internal revenue service
do not use this form to transmit electronically
rules.ruleOrLimit: Form 1096 goes only with paper forms.
rules.hangsApplication: HANGS must e-file, so no Form 1096 is filed. The draft shows the same totals as a transmittal summary for the reviewer: 9 forms, box 1a $708,088.00, box 4 $2,112.00.
rules.sourceTitle: About Form 1096, Annual Summary and Transmittal of U.S. Information Returns

rules.question: Which vendors are left out as corporations, merchandise or card payments?
rules.whyItMatters: Payments to C and S corporations, payments for merchandise and payments by card are not reported on Form 1099-NEC; the W-9 classification decides who is a corporation.
rules.effective: Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026), Exceptions and Form 1099-K.
rules.excerpt: Generally, payments to a corporation (including an LLC) that is treated as a C or S corporation). ... Payments for merchandise, telegrams, telephone, freight, storage, and similar items. ... Payments made with a credit card or payment card ... must be reported on Form 1099-K by the payment settlement entity under section 6050W and are not subject to reporting on Form 1099-MISC or Form 1099-NEC.
matchPhrases: generally, payments to a corporation (including an llc) that is treated as a c or s corporation)
payments for merchandise, telegrams, telephone, freight, storage, and similar items
must be reported on form 1099-k by the payment settlement entity under section 6050w and are not subject to reporting on form 1099-misc or form 1099-nec
rules.pageOrSection: Specific Instructions for Form 1099-NEC, Exceptions; Reminders, Form 1099-K
rules.ruleOrLimit: Leave out C and S corporations (an LLC by its tax classification) other than for legal services, payments for merchandise, and payments by card.
rules.hangsApplication: Left out: Northline Drywall Inc., Puget Sound Shoring Co. and Elliott Bay Equipment Rental Inc. (C corporations) and Evergreen Site Services LLC (an LLC taxed as an S corporation), $1,291,045.00; Olympic Lumber Supply LLC, lumber delivered with no services, $129,997.47; and Summit Crane and Rigging's two corporate card charges, $6,200.00. Cascade Rebar Placement LLC is a single-member LLC and is reported.
hangsFactsUsed: Vendor master (W-9 classification, exempt payee code)

rules.question: How are payments to the law firm and to the claimant's attorney reported?
rules.whyItMatters: Legal fees are reported even when the firm is a corporation; gross proceeds paid to an attorney, as in a settlement, go on Form 1099-MISC box 10 at $600, not on Form 1099-NEC.
rules.effective: Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026), Payments to attorneys.
rules.excerpt: Attorneys' fees of $2,000 or more paid in the course of your trade or business are reportable in box 1a of Form 1099-NEC ... The exemption from reporting payments made to corporations does not apply to payments for legal services. ... report in box 10 payments that: Are made to an attorney in the course of your trade or business in connection with legal services, but not for the attorney's services, for example, as in a settlement agreement; Total $600 or more
matchPhrases: attorneys' fees of $2,000 or more paid in the course of your trade or business are reportable in box 1a of form 1099-nec
the exemption from reporting payments made to corporations does not apply to payments for legal services
are made to an attorney in the course of your trade or business in connection with legal services, but not for the attorney's services, for example, as in a settlement agreement
total $600 or more
rules.pageOrSection: Payments to attorneys; Gross proceeds paid to attorneys; Payments to corporations for legal services
rules.ruleOrLimit: Fees for legal services: Form 1099-NEC box 1a at $2,000, corporations included. Gross proceeds paid to an attorney: Form 1099-MISC box 10 at $600.
rules.hangsApplication: Harbor Field Counsel PLLC is an LLC taxed as a C corporation, but its $38,640.00 of legal fees are reported in box 1a. The $85,000.00 settlement paid to Moss and Tarrant PLLC's client trust account is gross proceeds for Form 1099-MISC box 10, which this run does not prepare (MISC-01).

rules.question: Does the office rent go on Form 1099-NEC?
rules.whyItMatters: Rent is not compensation for services: it goes on Form 1099-MISC box 1.
rules.effective: Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026), Specific Instructions for Form 1099-MISC.
matchPhrases: at least $2,000 in: rents ( box 1 )
rules.ruleOrLimit: Rents of $2,000 or more go on Form 1099-MISC box 1.
rules.hangsApplication: The $96,000.00 of 2026 office rent to Harbor Ridge Office Partners LLC, a single-member LLC, belongs on Form 1099-MISC box 1, not on Form 1099-NEC (MISC-01).

rules.question: What did HANGS owe for the vendor that never gave a TIN?
rules.whyItMatters: Reportable payments to a payee with no TIN are subject to 24% backup withholding from the first payment; a payer that does not withhold becomes liable for it.
rules.effective: Instructions for the Requester of Form W-9 (Rev. March 2024), Reminders and Purpose.
rules.excerpt: The backup withholding rate is 24% for reportable payments. ... If you don't collect backup withholding from affected payees as required, you may become liable for any uncollected amount.
matchPhrases: the backup withholding rate is 24% for reportable payments
if you don't collect backup withholding from affected payees as required, you may become liable for any uncollected amount
rules.pageOrSection: Reminders: Backup withholding rate; Backup withholding liability
rules.ruleOrLimit: Withhold 24% of each reportable payment to a payee without a TIN until the TIN is furnished; an uncollected amount becomes the payer's liability.
rules.hangsApplication: Ridgeline Concrete Cutting gave no W-9 for any of its five payments, $14,400.00. 24% of every payment is $3,456.00; accounts payable withheld only from April 30 on, $2,112.00, which goes in box 4. The $1,344.00 not withheld from the February 27 and March 31 payments is HANGS's own liability (BACKUP-01).
rules.unresolved: A person reports and pays the backup withholding on Form 945, the uncollected $1,344.00 included (BACKUP-01).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for the Requester of Form W-9 (03/2024)

rules.question: From when must backup withholding start, and where is it reported?
rules.whyItMatters: Missing a TIN starts withholding at once, not after a set number of requests; the withheld tax is reported on Form 945 and in box 4.
rules.effective: General Instructions for Certain Information Returns, part N.
rules.excerpt: Failure to furnish TIN in the manner required. Withhold on payments made until the TIN is furnished in the manner required. ... Report backup withholding on Form 945, Annual Return of Withheld Federal Income Tax.
matchPhrases: withhold on payments made until the tin is furnished in the manner required
report backup withholding on form 945, annual return of withheld federal income tax
rules.ruleOrLimit: Withhold from the first reportable payment until a TIN is furnished; report the withholding on Form 945 and on the Form 1099-NEC.
rules.hangsApplication: Ridgeline's first payment, $2,400.00 on February 27, already met the $2,000 threshold, so withholding was due from it; accounts payable set it up only on April 20, after a third request.
rules.sourceTitle: General Instructions for Certain Information Returns

rules.question: What is wrong with the Cedar Hollow Tile W-9?
rules.whyItMatters: A sole proprietor's W-9 must carry the owner's own name on line 1; the business name on line 1 with the owner's SSN does not match IRS records.
rules.excerpt: (For a sole proprietor or disregarded entity, enter the owner's name on line 1, and enter the business/disregarded entity's name on line 2.)
matchPhrases: (for a sole proprietor or disregarded entity, enter the owner's name on line 1, and enter the business/disregarded entity's name on line 2.)
rules.ruleOrLimit: A sole proprietor puts the owner's name on line 1 and the business name on line 2.
rules.hangsApplication: Cedar Hollow Tile's W-9 has the business name on line 1 with an SSN, and IRS TIN Matching on October 21, 2026 found no match. The draft reports $26,850.00 under the name and TIN on file; a corrected W-9 was requested October 22 and has not come back (TIN-01).
rules.unresolved: A person gets the corrected W-9 before filing (TIN-01).
rules.sourceTitle: Form W-9 (Rev. March 2024), Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification

rules.question: Is Tomas Arvelo, paid by the hour through accounts payable, a contractor for Form 1099-NEC or an employee for Form W-2?
rules.whyItMatters: Form 1099-NEC is only for someone who is not an employee. An employee's pay belongs on Form W-2 with withholding.
rules.effective: The IRS page, saved copy retrieved November 5, 2026.
rules.excerpt: In determining whether the person providing service is an employee or an independent contractor, all information that provides evidence of the degree of control and independence must be considered. ... If you classify an employee as an independent contractor and you have no reasonable basis for doing so, then you may be held liable for employment taxes for that worker
matchPhrases: all information that provides evidence of the degree of control and independence must be considered
if you classify an employee as an independent contractor and you have no reasonable basis for doing so, then you may be held liable for employment taxes for that worker
rules.ruleOrLimit: Whether a worker is an employee turns on the right to direct and control the work.
rules.hangsApplication: Tomas Arvelo was paid $33,348.00 in 2026 for 794 hours of concrete finishing at $42.00 an hour under the HGC foreman at Tideflats Cold Storage, the question left open by the Q3 Form 941 review. The draft reports him on Form 1099-NEC as accounts payable recorded him (LABOR-01).
hangsFactsUsed: 2026 vendor payments (hours and rate in the descriptions)
rules.unresolved: A person decides the worker's status before filing (LABOR-01).

changes.note: For payments after 2025 the Form 1099-NEC threshold is $2,000 instead of $600, adjusted for inflation from 2027; gross proceeds paid to attorneys stay at $600. Forms 1099-NEC also gain boxes 1b to 1d for cash tips and overtime, none of which apply to these payees.
